items.a: No. It is a Draft. It moved to Review on 2025-10-08, and an EIP editor returned it to Draft on 2026-01-13. It was still Draft on 2026-10-18, even though registries are listed on 25 mainnets in the contracts README (on Soneium the proxies still ran a placeholder that day).

items.q: Does ERC-8004 move money or pay agents?
items.a: No. The text calls payments orthogonal, and the registries have no function that takes or forwards payments; the only payable entry point is the owner-only upgradeToAndCall. x402 or another rail moves the money; ERC-8004 only publishes the payee address and lets feedback point to a payment.

No. The Identity and Reputation registries are listed on 25 mainnets. The Validation Registry is specified, but the contracts README lists no address for it; a contract answers at a scripted address on Ethereum and Base but is not announced, so treat it as not officially deployed.

items.q: Does an agent have to authorize feedback with feedbackAuth?
items.a: Not any more. The agent-signed feedbackAuth was removed from the contracts on 2025-11-12 and from the text on 2026-01-07. Any address except the owner and operators can rate an agent.

items.q: Does a large number of registered agents mean the ecosystem is healthy?
items.a: No. Agent count is not agent quality. Ids cost only gas to mint (no fee) and include placeholders; one study found only 3% to 15% of agents with a valid file and a live endpoint (data to 2026-05-13), and a census found at least 13,210 of 505,635 ids declaring an http(s) endpoint, with 231,014 files not fetched (2026-09-26).

Only in the off-chain feedback file. The registry stores value, decimals, two tags and the revoked flag; it never stores or checks the payment proof. Upload the file first, then call giveFeedback with its URI and hash.

items.q: Why does getSummary need a list of client addresses?
items.a: Because unfiltered feedback is open to Sybil and spam attacks. The reader must choose reviewers it trusts, and the reference code reverts with an empty list.

items.q: What happens to the agent wallet when the agent token is sold?
items.a: The transfer clears agentWallet, and the new owner must bind a wallet again with a signature from that wallet.

Only the contract owner. On Ethereum and Base on 2026-10-11 that was one externally owned account, not a multisig contract, and the holder is not published. On BSC the owners differ: a Safe multisig for Identity and Reputation and an EIP-7702 account for the Validation proxy.

items.q: Is ERC-8004 the same as ERC-8183 or ERC-8126?
items.a: No. ERC-8183 is job escrow with an evaluator and ERC-8126 is a verification standard that requires ERC-8004. ERC-8126 reached Final on 2026-06-02 while ERC-8004 stays Draft.

items.q: Is the ERC-8004 Identity Registry the same thing as the ERC-3643 Identity Registry?
items.a: No. The T-REX registry maps wallets to verified identities and countries for token transfers. The ERC-8004 registry is an open ERC-721 directory of agents. In ERC-3643 an Agent is an operator role, not an AI agent.

items.q: Does ERC-8004 check who runs an agent?
items.a: No. Registration is permissionless and has no KYC or know-your-agent step, and the text cannot cryptographically guarantee that advertised capabilities work.
